card.title: Why a longer pain can feel better

body.question: Trial 1: hand in 14 degree Celsius water for 60 seconds. Trial 2: 60 seconds the same, then 30 more seconds as the water is warmed to 15 degrees. Which trial were people more willing to repeat?
body.reveal: Trial 2, despite the extra exposure. The researchers concluded people liked the memory of it better. In a colonoscopy study, patients likewise judged discomfort by the worst moment (peak) and the final moments (end), regardless of how long it lasted.

probes.question: According to the peak-end rule, which moments dominate how an experience is remembered?
True or false: in the colonoscopy study, patients' discomfort ratings depended mainly on how long the procedure lasted.

claims.claim: Trial 1: hand in 14 C water for 60 seconds
claims.quote: The first trial had subjects submerge a hand in 14 °C water for 60 seconds.

claims.claim: Trial 2: same 60 seconds, then 30 more seconds as the water was warmed to 15 C
claims.quote: but then keep their hand submerged for an additional 30 seconds, during which the temperature was raised to 15 °C

claims.claim: People were more willing to repeat Trial 2 despite longer exposure
claims.quote: subjects were more willing to repeat the second trial, despite a prolonged exposure to uncomfortable temperatures

claims.claim: Researchers concluded people liked the memory of it better
claims.quote: subjects chose the long trial simply because they liked the memory of it better than the alternative

claims.claim: Colonoscopy study: patients judged discomfort by worst moment (peak) and final moments (end)
claims.quote: They found that patients consistently evaluated the discomfort of the experience based on the intensity of pain at the worst (peak) and final (end) moments

claims.claim: ...regardless of how long it lasted (probe 2: ratings did not depend mainly on duration)
claims.quote: This occurred regardless of length or variation in intensity of pain within the procedure.

claims.claim: Peak-end rule: peak and end dominate how an experience is judged (probe 1)
claims.quote: people judge an experience largely based on how they felt at its peak
